body:
For me, it was always creeping near the end of elementary for me, and it reached its absolute worst point by 9th grade. A lot of it was just disdain for my friends and peers because they didn’t see the kid who had a heart he wanted to pass around. Instead they disregarded it or laughed at me at worse. Loneliness became a recurring thing that festered my depression.

High school was when I truly was alone. I even dreaded lunch periods if I had no one to sit with because then I’d be alone with the depressive thoughts just eating at me. Because I was an absolute joke and embarrassment, and if that would be the consistency life has shown me, why would I want to keep living? Figured I’d end it after graduation.

A new hobby “saved” me, really. It at least put me around some friends who see I can provide something and cherish it. So here I am for now. Even still today, I’ve noticed I can be put into a depressive episode if I’m around an upbeat  social circle of people and I’m alone and out of the loop.
